title: A tensor-counit transpose under an adjunction mate
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal C',\mathcal D'$ be monoidal categories [def-nagata-category, def-sfb-monoidal-category, def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be left adjoint to $G$, and $F':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$ left adjoint to $G'$, with counits $\varepsilon,\varepsilon'$ and the usual triangle identities [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Let $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, $H':\mathcal D'\to\mathcal C'$, $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$, and $V:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ be strong monoidal functors, and fix a monoidal natural isomorphism $UH\cong H'V$. All expressions below use these tensor, composition and unit comparisons. Let $\beta:VF\xrightarrow{\sim}F'U$ be a natural isomorphism and define $e_K:UGK\to G'VK$ as the adjoint transpose of $V\varepsilon_K\circ\beta_{GK}^{-1}$.

Suppose given projection transformations $P(K,M):K\otimes FM\to F(HK\otimes M)$ and $P'(K',M'):K'\otimes F'M'\to F'(H'K'\otimes M')$, natural in both arguments. Fix $K\in\mathcal D$. Assume these maps are invertible at $(K,G\mathbf1)$, $(VK,UG\mathbf1)$ and $(VK,G'\mathbf1)$, and write $q(K,G\mathbf1)$ and the corresponding $q'$ for their inverses. Assume at $M=G\mathbf1$ the projection/exchange equation
$$(1_{VK}\otimes\beta_M)Vq(K,M)\beta_{HK\otimes M}^{-1}=q'(VK,UM).$$
Put $\omega=G\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$, $\omega'=G'\mathbf1_{\mathcal D'}$, and let $e_1:U\omega\to\omega'$ be the component of $e$ at the unit, using $V\mathbf1\cong\mathbf1$. Let $t_K:HK\otimes\omega\to GK$ and $t'_{VK}:H'VK\otimes\omega'\to G'VK$ be the transposes of $(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_1)q(K,\omega)$ and $(1_{VK}\otimes\varepsilon'_1)q'(VK,\omega')$, with right unitors understood. Then
$$e_K\circ U(t_K)=t'_{VK}\circ(1_{H'VK}\otimes e_1),$$
where the source on the left is identified with $H'VK\otimes U\omega$. In particular both transposes under $F'\dashv G'$ are the map
$$(1_{VK}\otimes(V\varepsilon_1\circ\beta_\omega^{-1}))\circ q'(VK,U\omega):F'(H'VK\otimes U\omega)\to VK.$$
The same implication holds for adjunctions restricted to full subcategories of these monoidal categories whenever every displayed object and map lies in the domains of the specified adjunction Hom bijections; it requires no invertibility of $e_1$ and no faithfulness of any evaluation functor.

proof.text: Write $A=HK\otimes\omega$, $B=H' VK\otimes U\omega$ (so $B=UA$ by the specified comparisons), and $h=1_{H' VK}\otimes e_1$. For an arrow $x:B\to G\prime VK$, its inverse adjunction transpose is $T\prime(x)=\varepsilon\prime_{VK}\circ F\prime(x)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Put $a=(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_1)q(K,\omega)$ and $a\prime=(1_{VK}\otimes\varepsilon\prime_1)q\prime(VK,\omega\prime)$. The defining transpose equations give $\varepsilon_K\circ F(t_K)=a$ and $\varepsilon\prime_{VK}\circ F\prime(t\prime_{VK})=a\prime$.

source.place: Proof (2), tensor map: expand the two transposes

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] with left square $\beta^{-1}$ and mate $e$: $\varepsilon\prime_{VK}\circ F\prime(e_K)=V(\varepsilon_K)\circ\beta_{GK}^{-1}$. Naturality of $\beta^{-1}$ at $t_K:A\to GK$ says $\beta_{GK}^{-1}\circ F\prime U(t_K)=VF(t_K)\circ\beta_A^{-1}$. Substitute these two equations and the preceding transpose equation to obtain $$T\prime(e_K\circ U(t_K))=V(a)\circ\beta_A^{-1}.$$ All terms here have source $F\prime(UA)$ and target $VK$.

source.place: Proof (2), tensor map: expand the two transposes

proof.text: By tensorator naturality and unit compatibility in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], $V(a)=(1_{VK}\otimes V\varepsilon_1)Vq(K,\omega)$ under the stipulated comparisons, with the right unitor included. The assumed projection/exchange equation at $M=\omega$ gives $$Vq(K,\omega)\beta_A^{-1}=(1_{VK}\otimes\beta_\omega^{-1})q\prime(VK,U\omega).$$ Compose and use functoriality of tensor [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Thus the transpose in step 2 equals $$c=(1_{VK}\otimes(V\varepsilon_1\circ\beta_\omega^{-1}))q\prime(VK,U\omega).$$

source.place: Proof (2), tensor map: expand the two transposes

proof.text: Use naturality of $P\prime$ in its second argument at $e_1:U\omega\to\omega\prime$: $$P\prime(VK,\omega\prime)(1_{VK}\otimes F\prime e_1)=F\prime(h)P\prime(VK,U\omega).$$ Multiplying on the left by $q\prime(VK,\omega\prime)$ and on the right by $q\prime(VK,U\omega)$ yields $$q\prime(VK,\omega\prime)F\prime(h)=(1_{VK}\otimes F\prime e_1)q\prime(VK,U\omega).$$ Therefore step 1 and tensor functoriality [def-sfb-monoidal-category] give $$T\prime(t\prime_{VK}\circ h)=(1_{VK}\otimes(\varepsilon\prime_1\circ F\prime e_1))q\prime(VK,U\omega).$$ The mate counit equation [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] at $1_{\mathcal D}$ identifies $\varepsilon\prime_1\circ F\prime e_1=V\varepsilon_1\circ\beta_\omega^{-1}$ under $V1\cong1$. Explicitly, for $v:V1\to1$, $e_1=G\prime(v)e_{1_{\mathcal D}}$, and counit naturality moves $F\prime G\prime(v)$ past $\varepsilon\prime_1$. Consequently this transpose is also $c$.

source.place: Proof (2), tensor map: expand the two transposes

proof.text: The inverse Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] is injective. Steps 2--4 show that it sends both arrows to $c$, so the arrows are equal and their common transpose is the displayed map in the statement. The calculation uses only compositions, the two assumed projection inverses for $P\prime$, the assumed exchange equation, and adjunction Hom bijections. In full subcategories all the same equalities hold whenever the displayed objects and maps belong to the specified Hom domains. No inverse of $e_1$ and no evaluation functor occurs.
